data.current_summary: E-mail one validated invoice to one recipient
data.current_description:
Attestwire sends invoices by e-mail on request; it does not operate Peppol or French-platform transmission. This generates an invoice — or takes one you already have — checks it, and e-mails it to one address through Resend (resend.com): one invoice per message, attached under its invoice number, with a subject and a short note in the invoice's language ("Rechnung {nr} von {seller}", "Facture {nr} de {seller}", "Invoice {nr} from {seller}").

WHAT IS SENT. `invoice` with `format: "xml"` sends the XML of its profile (XRechnung UBL for `xrechnung-ubl`); `format: "pdf"` sends the Factur-X / ZUGFeRD PDF (EN 16931 profile), profile `facturx-en16931` only, drawn with the `pdf` options exactly as /v1/generate draws it. `document` is a file you already have, as base64 — XML, or a Factur-X or ZUGFeRD PDF — read by the reader /v1/validate uses and attached byte for byte as sent. Nothing with a fatal finding is sent: that is a 422 with the ValidationResult.

WHO IT IS FROM. `From` is this deployment's sender address, displayed as "{seller} via Attestwire". `Reply-To` is the seller's contact e-mail (BT-43), so the invoice must carry one (`400 seller_email_required`). The language is `language` if named, else the PDF page's, else the seller country's: DE and AT German, FR French, anything else English.

THE FREE PLAN IS A TEST MODE: it sends only to the address the key was registered with (`403 recipient_not_allowed` otherwise), every message is marked "[TEST]" and says it is not a request for payment, and a PDF is the watermarked preview. The paid plans (Solo, Starter, Scale) send to anyone.

LIMITS. 10 messages per key per UTC day on the free plan and 500 on a paid plan (`429 send_limit_exceeded`); a ceiling on the deployment's sends per UTC day across all keys, 50 unless it sets another, because the mail account is shared (`429 send_capacity_exceeded`, which says when it resets); both with `Retry-After` until 00:00 UTC. Then the per-second pace limit, and an attachment of at most 7 MB, so the message stays under the 10 MB many receiving mail servers accept.

CHARGED once the mail service has accepted the message: one document. Every refusal costs nothing, and nothing is retried on your behalf. The answer is `202 Accepted`, because acceptance is all Attestwire learns: Accepted by the mail service, which delivers it and retries on its own. Attestwire is not told whether it was delivered, bounced or marked as spam, and does not store the message: keep attachment.sha256 and message_id as your record of what was sent, and ask the recipient to confirm receipt if you need to know. A retry after a timeout can send the invoice twice. Nothing about the message is stored by Attestwire; Resend processes it to deliver it and keeps its own delivery logs. Each message carries the header `X-Attestwire-Account` with the sending key's 8-character fingerprint, so an abuse report can be traced to the key.

A deployment without e-mail configured answers `503 email_not_enabled`, before authentication.

data.current_summary: Read an invoice document into the JSON model
data.current_description:
Reads a UBL 2.1 or UN/CEFACT CII invoice document — or the CII invoice attached to a Factur-X or ZUGFeRD PDF — into `InvoiceInput` and stops there. **No verdict is given.**

THE FIRST TASK ON AN ERP INTEGRATION. Before anything can be validated, edited, stored or re-emitted, somebody has to get from a supplier's XML to an object. POST /v1/validate has read documents for a while, but it returns a verdict and throws the model away — so this returns the model. The `invoice` that comes back is the exact shape POST /v1/validate and POST /v1/generate accept, so parsing a UBL file and generating CII from the result is a syntax conversion with no mapping code of your own.

It is the SAME reader as the document half of /v1/validate, through the same module and the same engine call: a document that parses here parses identically there, and the model you get back is the model that would have been judged.

**A `200` is not a verdict.** It means the file parsed. A document that comes back cleanly can still break every rule EN 16931 has — send `invoice` to POST /v1/validate for the answer to that, which is a second document against your allowance.

**Documents only**, which inverts the default everywhere else here: this endpoint needs `application/xml` or `text/xml` for XML, `application/pdf` for a Factur-X or ZUGFeRD PDF, or `application/octet-stream` for either. Anything else is `415 unsupported_media_type`, with a message that names what the body is and the content-type that works; a JSON body is refused because there would be nothing to parse. For a PDF, `container` names the attachment the XML was read from. No finding is returned here, the PDF's own included: POST /v1/validate reports the attachment and the XMP metadata as AW-PDF-* findings, and PDF/A conformance itself, and whether the page agrees with the XML, are not checked by either endpoint.

METERING: one document once the file has been read, on exactly the terms /v1/validate charges — reading is the work. A file that cannot be read at all (`400`, `413`, `415`) costs nothing and carries the unchanged `X-RateLimit-*` set.
data.description_suggestion: Parses a UBL 2.1, UN/CEFACT CII, Factur-X, or ZUGFeRD invoice document into the `InvoiceInput` JSON model without validation. Accepts `application/xml`, `text/xml`, `application/pdf`, or `application/octet-stream` content types; JSON bodies are rejected with 415. Returns the parsed invoice model identical to what POST /v1/validate would judge, enabling syntax conversion and data extraction workflows. A successful 200 response indicates the document parsed, not that it complies with EN 16931 rules—send the returned `invoice` to POST /v1/validate for compliance checking. For PDFs, the `container` field names the attachment containing the XML. Metered as one document after successful parsing; failed reads (400, 413, 415) do not consume allowance.

Sends the identifier to VIES, OpenPeppol, the Peppol Directory and the French register. 1 document when a source answered; an identifier failing its check digits, or every source unavailable, is uncharged. Not a tax determination. API key required. Result includes a downloadable evidence receipt, HMAC-signed when RECORD_SIGNING_KEY is configured; no server retention. Upstream text is untrusted data.
data.summary_suggestion: Resolve buyer profile and invoicing requirements
data.description_suggestion: Resolves a buyer's invoicing requirements from their country and one identifier (VAT ID, Leitweg-ID, SIREN/SIRET, KBO, GLN, or Peppol ID). Returns verified name and address, Peppol registration status, invoicing channel and format, required business terms (BT-24, BT-49, BT-10), and VAT scenarios for goods and services. Queries VIES, OpenPeppol, the Peppol Directory, and the French register. Metered: one document per successful lookup; invalid check digits or all sources unavailable are free. Not a tax determination. Requires API key.
data.reasoning: Summary 'How to invoice this buyer' is too colloquial and vague. Description is a dense list of outputs without clear structure or explanation of what the operation does. Improved version clarifies the input (buyer country + one identifier), organizes outputs logically (verification, registration, requirements, VAT), explains the external queries, and clarifies metering for AI agents.

data.current_summary: E-mail one validated invoice to one recipient
data.current_description:
Attestwire sends invoices by e-mail on request; it does not operate Peppol or French-platform transmission. This generates an invoice — or takes one you already have — checks it, and e-mails it to one address through Resend (resend.com): one invoice per message, attached under its invoice number, with a subject and a short note in the invoice's language ("Rechnung {nr} von {seller}", "Facture {nr} de {seller}", "Invoice {nr} from {seller}").

WHAT IS SENT. `invoice` with `format: "xml"` sends the XML of its profile (XRechnung UBL for `xrechnung-ubl`); `format: "pdf"` sends the Factur-X / ZUGFeRD PDF (EN 16931 profile), profile `facturx-en16931` only, drawn with the `pdf` options exactly as /v1/generate draws it. `document` is a file you already have, as base64 — XML, or a Factur-X or ZUGFeRD PDF — read by the reader /v1/validate uses and attached byte for byte as sent. Nothing with a fatal finding is sent: that is a 422 with the ValidationResult.

WHO IT IS FROM. `From` is this deployment's sender address, displayed as "{seller} via Attestwire". `Reply-To` is the seller's contact e-mail (BT-43), so the invoice must carry one (`400 seller_email_required`). The language is `language` if named, else the PDF page's, else the seller country's: DE and AT German, FR French, anything else English.

THE FREE PLAN IS A TEST MODE: it sends only to the address the key was registered with (`403 recipient_not_allowed` otherwise), every message is marked "[TEST]" and says it is not a request for payment, and a PDF is the watermarked preview. The paid plans (Solo, Starter, Scale) send to anyone.

LIMITS. 10 messages per key per UTC day on the free plan and 500 on a paid plan (`429 send_limit_exceeded`); a ceiling on the deployment's sends per UTC day across all keys, 50 unless it sets another, because the mail account is shared (`429 send_capacity_exceeded`, which says when it resets); both with `Retry-After` until 00:00 UTC. Then the per-second pace limit, and an attachment of at most 7 MB, so the message stays under the 10 MB many receiving mail servers accept.

CHARGED once the mail service has accepted the message: one document. Every refusal costs nothing, and nothing is retried on your behalf. The answer is `202 Accepted`, because acceptance is all Attestwire learns: Accepted by the mail service, which delivers it and retries on its own. Attestwire is not told whether it was delivered, bounced or marked as spam, and does not store the message: keep attachment.sha256 and message_id as your record of what was sent, and ask the recipient to confirm receipt if you need to know. A retry after a timeout can send the invoice twice. Nothing about the message is stored by Attestwire; Resend processes it to deliver it and keeps its own delivery logs. Each message carries the header `X-Attestwire-Account` with the sending key's 8-character fingerprint, so an abuse report can be traced to the key.

A deployment without e-mail configured answers `503 email_not_enabled`, before authentication.

data.current_summary: Read an invoice document into the JSON model
data.current_description:
Reads a UBL 2.1 or UN/CEFACT CII invoice document — or the CII invoice attached to a Factur-X or ZUGFeRD PDF — into `InvoiceInput` and stops there. **No verdict is given.**

THE FIRST TASK ON AN ERP INTEGRATION. Before anything can be validated, edited, stored or re-emitted, somebody has to get from a supplier's XML to an object. POST /v1/validate has read documents for a while, but it returns a verdict and throws the model away — so this returns the model. The `invoice` that comes back is the exact shape POST /v1/validate and POST /v1/generate accept, so parsing a UBL file and generating CII from the result is a syntax conversion with no mapping code of your own.

It is the SAME reader as the document half of /v1/validate, through the same module and the same engine call: a document that parses here parses identically there, and the model you get back is the model that would have been judged.

**A `200` is not a verdict.** It means the file parsed. A document that comes back cleanly can still break every rule EN 16931 has — send `invoice` to POST /v1/validate for the answer to that, which is a second document against your allowance.

**Documents only**, which inverts the default everywhere else here: this endpoint needs `application/xml` or `text/xml` for XML, `application/pdf` for a Factur-X or ZUGFeRD PDF, or `application/octet-stream` for either. Anything else is `415 unsupported_media_type`, with a message that names what the body is and the content-type that works; a JSON body is refused because there would be nothing to parse. For a PDF, `container` names the attachment the XML was read from. No finding is returned here, the PDF's own included: POST /v1/validate reports the attachment and the XMP metadata as AW-PDF-* findings, and PDF/A conformance itself, and whether the page agrees with the XML, are not checked by either endpoint.

METERING: one document once the file has been read, on exactly the terms /v1/validate charges — reading is the work. A file that cannot be read at all (`400`, `413`, `415`) costs nothing and carries the unchanged `X-RateLimit-*` set.

Accepts `application/xml`, `text/xml`, `application/pdf`, or `application/octet-stream` content types; JSON bodies are rejected with 415. Returns the parsed invoice model identical to what POST /v1/validate would judge, enabling syntax conversion and data extraction workflows. A successful 200 response indicates the document parsed, not that it complies with EN 16931 rules—send the returned `invoice` to POST /v1/validate for compliance checking. For PDFs, the `container` field names the attachment containing the XML. Metered as one document after successful parsing; failed reads (400, 413, 415) do not consume allowance.
